title: Conversion (functional neurologic) disorder after acute stress
vignette: A 40-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by her roommate due to significant left leg weakness. The symptom began 3 days ago after her father had a heart attack. There is no personal or family history of neurological disease; surgical history includes liposuction of the thighs and varicose vein removal. She does not use tobacco, alcohol, or illicit drugs. Temperature is 36.7 C (98.1 F), blood pressure is 123/81 mm Hg, pulse is 62/min, and respirations are 14/min. Physical examination reveals symmetric 2+ deep tendon reflexes as well as normal muscle bulk and tone bilaterally in the upper and lower extremities. Laboratory testing and neurologic imaging reveal no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

clues.note: A dramatic neurologic deficit (leg weakness) is the presenting symptom; the key is whether exam/workup support a real neurologic lesion.

clues.text: began 3 days ago after her father had a heart attack
clues.note: Onset of a neurologic symptom immediately after an acute psychological stressor is highly characteristic of conversion (functional neurologic symptom) disorder.

clues.text: symmetric 2+ deep tendon reflexes as well as normal muscle bulk and tone
clues.note: Normal reflexes, bulk, and tone are INCOMPATIBLE with a genuine motor lesion causing true weakness - the deficit is functional.

clues.text: Laboratory testing and neurologic imaging reveal no abnormalities
clues.note: A completely negative workup supports a functional (conversion) disorder rather than an identifiable neurologic disease.

whatMatters: Acute neurologic weakness triggered by a psychological stressor, with an exam and workup INCOMPATIBLE with any organic lesion (normal reflexes/tone/bulk, normal imaging) = CONVERSION DISORDER (functional neurologic symptom disorder). The symptoms are not consciously produced. Answer B.
strategy: Match to DSM criteria: conversion disorder = neurologic symptom incompatible with recognized disease, often after stress, not intentionally produced. Reject somatic symptom disorder (excessive thoughts about real symptoms, no incompatibility), illness anxiety (fear of disease, minimal symptoms), factitious disorder (intentional falsification for the sick role), malingering (intentional for external gain), and body dysmorphic disorder (preoccupation with appearance).

eliminations.label: Body dysmorphic disorder - preoccupation with appearance
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: excessive preoccupation with a perceived physical defect in appearance. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this patient has a neurologic deficit, not a concern about how she looks. ✅ Correct if: distress/rituals over a perceived flaw (e.g., nose shape).

eliminations.label: Factitious disorder - intentional, for the sick role
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: deliberate falsification/induction of symptoms to assume the sick role (internal motivation). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: there is no evidence she is intentionally faking; conversion symptoms are unconsciously produced. ✅ Correct if: covert self-induced illness without external reward.

eliminations.label: Illness anxiety disorder - fear of disease, minimal symptoms
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: preoccupation with HAVING a serious illness despite minimal or no somatic symptoms. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this patient has a prominent physical symptom (leg weakness), not health anxiety about a feared disease. ✅ Correct if: a patient fixated on having cancer despite normal findings.

eliminations.label: Malingering - intentional, for external gain
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: conscious symptom falsification for an obvious external incentive (money, disability, avoiding work). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: no secondary gain is described, and conversion symptoms are not consciously produced. ✅ Correct if: feigning to obtain disability benefits/avoid duty.

eliminations.label: Somatic symptom disorder - excessive thoughts about real symptoms
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: one or more distressing somatic symptoms with excessive, persistent thoughts/anxiety and health-related behaviors. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: the defining feature of THIS case is a deficit INCOMPATIBLE with neurologic disease (conversion), and she voices no excessive health anxiety (she was brought in by her roommate). ✅ Correct if: chronic multiple symptoms with disproportionate worry.

reasoning: Acute left leg weakness beginning right after a major psychological stressor
Exam (normal reflexes/tone/bulk) and imaging/labs are INCOMPATIBLE with a true neurologic lesion
This incompatibility + stress trigger + unconscious production = conversion disorder
mechanism: Conversion disorder (functional neurologic symptom disorder) presents with neurologic symptoms - weakness/paralysis, sensory loss, blindness, aphonia, or nonepileptic 'seizures' - that are INCOMPATIBLE with any recognized neurologic or medical condition. A hallmark is internal inconsistency on examination (e.g., normal reflexes, tone, and muscle bulk despite 'paralysis'; give-way weakness; a positive Hoover sign) and a negative diagnostic workup. Symptoms often begin acutely after a psychological stressor (here, the father's heart attack) and are NOT intentionally produced - distinguishing conversion from factitious disorder (intentional, for the sick role) and malingering (intentional, for external gain). Although 'la belle indifference' (incongruent lack of concern) is described, it is neither sensitive nor specific and should not be used to make the diagnosis; patients may be quite distressed. Management centers on reassurance, education, and often physical therapy/psychotherapy.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Psych > somatic symptom & related disorders: conversion (functional neurologic, incompatible with disease, unconscious), somatic symptom (excessive thoughts about real symptoms), illness anxiety, factitious (sick role), malingering (external gain).

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: The exam/imaging incompatibility plus a stress trigger and no intentional production define conversion disorder.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on conversion/functional neurologic disorder, la belle indifference, Hoover sign, or factitious vs malingering? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Somatic symptom disorder = excessive worry about REAL symptoms (no incompatibility); factitious/malingering are intentional; illness anxiety = fear with minimal symptoms.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: conversion disorder = neuro symptom incompatible with disease, often post-stress, NOT consciously produced; reassure + PT/psychotherapy.

Intentional symptoms for the sick role (no external reward)
Excessive thoughts/anxiety about real somatic symptoms
Preoccupation with having a serious illness, minimal symptoms
Unreliable sign sometimes seen in conversion disorder

memoryHook: Weakness that appears the moment life turns stressful but vanishes on exam and imaging - the body 'converts' distress into a deficit it isn't consciously faking.
